Move design: rules/moves.rs. Move = Game{at, payload} | Battle{at, card_uuid} | Json(Value); Payload = Empty | Uuid | Attack{uuid,target} | DonBox{uuid,target_ids,don_k} | Json(Value). to_json() rebuilds exactly the dicts the old code built (same key order: kind, action_type, payload / card_uuid; uuid, target_ids, don_k). Accessors (action_type, kind, card_uuid, payload().uuid / first_target_id / has_target_ids / don_k_i64 / don_k_f64 / first_selected / get) return the same values as the old Value::get(..).and_then(as_*) on both typed and Json forms. Equality = JSON equality: typed-vs-typed compares fields (the typed->JSON map is injective), anything involving Json compares to_json(). Moves coming in from Python (commit replay, search_apply, describe_move, apply_search_move) stay Json, so their re-serialization is byte-identical.

Boundary: Python-facing JSON is unchanged — decide output converts with to_json at search/mod.rs (move, stats.legal, pv), get_legal_actions (py_game / state.rs) maps the typed list to JSON, search_legal maps on output. rules::actions::apply_game_action(&Value) keeps its signature (thin wrapper over apply_game_action_with(GameArgs, payload)); the search's DON_BOX expansion passes the same uuid / target the old {"uuid"} / {"uuid","target_ids"} dicts yielded.

Decision-window listing: get_legal_moves / adapter::legal_actions use pending_actor_action (same branches and the same idempotent battle-phase normalization as get_pending_request) and build MULLIGAN / SELECT_BLOCKER / SELECT_COUNTER / MAIN moves from blocker_candidates / counter_candidates / main_actions directly — the exact functions get_pending_request uses for selectable_uuids. Interaction front actions never coincide with those four (checked InteractionKind::front_action), and selection_moves (dialog alternatives) returns None for them, so the merge step is a no-op there as before. Dialogs still build the pending JSON once (default payload + alternatives read it).

Drains (search/apply.rs and encode's on-play probe): the old code built the pending JSON only to read player_id / action / can_skip / selectable_uuids / constraints / intent / allow_* for selection_branch_exists and default_interaction_payload. These now read the same values from the active Interaction (selection_branch_exists_of, default_interaction_payload_of; the shared payload body is default_payload_from). Reached only for interaction actions (pending_actor_action checks mulligan, then the interaction, so any action other than the four decision kinds is the interaction's front_action).

Merge keys of dialog alternatives: the HashSet<String> of JSON-text keys became a linear scan with json_text_eq, which equals to_string() equality (arrays elementwise, numbers by text when a float is involved, dicts by text). Insertion order and first-wins are unchanged.

Caches of master-only facts (no change in what is read): AbilityTable.recalc_skip (is_reactive_passive || is_rest_replacement per ability, built once per table) and MasterTable.don_cond (don_cond_max_n of each card text; has_don_conditional == don_cond_max_n.is_some()). Both are OnceLock and fall back to computing on the spot if the table grew after the cache was built (only unit tests push to tables; production tables are immutable after load; with_extra_masters / without_abilities clones behave correctly via the length check / fresh default).

process_stack now borrows the node from the immutable master ability table instead of cloning the subtree each step; get_target_cards reads its 15 loop-invariant query flags once before the candidate loop; units()/units_with_stage presize; slot/uuid maps for candidate rows are presized only inside priors_keep (slot_index itself is unchanged because py_game serializes its iteration order); defense_box_prune checks kinds without a SipHash set; RESOLVE application does not parse uuid/target fields (only the payload is read in that arm; operating_card is a pure lookup).

Scope: WP rs-speed-d asked for the typed Move and allocation/copy cuts in legal generation (rules/legal.rs) and move application (search/apply.rs). I also touched rules/effects code that apply_move_inplace reaches (resolver, passives, matcher, interact, triggers, turn) and the two encoder call sites that consume legal-move lists — all listed in outputs.files_touched for the later merge with rs-speed-c. net/* was not touched. Possible merge overlap with rs-speed-c: search/quiesce.rs (priors_keep candidate-map presize, cand_owned/cand_parts) and encode/scalars.rs / encode/tokens.rs (only the legal-list / drain lines).

Not done / left for later (measured on the stage-2 callgrind): passive recalculation after every action (apply_passive_effects -> game_resolve_ability -> get_target_cards) is still ~9% of instructions; avoiding it needs an incremental/dirty-tracking scheme, which is a semantic change, not a copy cut.
